messages:
dave_customer: we keep getting truncated SSE streams after our client refreshes auth. final chunk is missing and the JSON ends mid-object, finish_reason never shows up.

maria_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the curl output + request headers you used? are you rotating the Authorization header while the stream is open?

dave_customer: yes, we rotate short-lived tokens and re-open the stream on refresh. logs show a 401 then immediate reconnect and 200. trimmed curl: 
```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream"```

jeff_runtime: any proxy in front (Fastly/nginx/Cloud CDN)? and can you include x-request-id or any trace id from the last chunk?

dave_customer: nginx 1.24 in front. nginx error log has: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream" right around the time of the token swap.

maria_support: when you rotate token, does the client reuse the same TCP connection or tear down and establish a new one?

dave_customer: we close and reconnect. we also attempt a resume using our own resume header, but the client sees a truncated JSON fragment and no final "data: [DONE]" event.

jeff_runtime: that sounds like a race where the proxy/RST prevents the backend from flushing the terminal chunk. can you reproduce without the nginx proxy (direct to api.redwood.ai)?

ops_bot: automated-test streaming-auth-rotation-repro started.

maria_support: short-term workaround: avoid rotating auth mid-stream (delay rotation until stream completes) or use a longer-lived stream token and rotate via a parallel control channel. we'll escalate to runtime for a deeper look.

jeff_runtime: please capture a tcpdump and the full request/response exchange (including the SSE frames). also include the x-request-id from the last visible SSE frame — that helps us find the backend trace.

dave_customer: repro steps I'm sharing: 
1) open SSE with token expiring in 30s
2) at 18s, client requests refreshed token and reconnects immediately
3) on reconnect the server responds 200 but the client receives a truncated JSON fragment and no terminal event.
We also see "finish_reason": null in the application logs for that stream.

maria_support: thanks — escalating now. tagging @jeff_runtime and runtime oncall. next steps: try direct (bypass nginx), provide tcpdump, and paste x-request-id values.

dave_customer: will DM the tcpdump and request IDs, thanks :pray:

ops_bot: incident created: SD-1279 streaming-auth-rotate-truncation

maria_support: assigned to runtime oncall, marking support escalate.
